text: Why can't we just drink seawater?
But seawater has over three times the salt of your blood.
Your kidneys can't make pee saltier than the sea, so flushing the salt costs more water than you drank.
The Gulf is hot desert with almost no rain, so it uses the sea anyway.
Desalination plants boil seawater and catch the steam, or push it through filters too fine for salt.
One Saudi plant makes a million cubic meters a day. About four hundred Olympic pools.
The Gulf holds a third of the world's desalination capacity. Kuwait relies on it almost completely.
The catch? It burns lots of energy, and the leftover brine can hurt the sea.
So yes, you can drink the sea. You just need a very big plant.
